def-it-information-units-and-logarithm-b:
## Definition

Write $\ln$ for the natural logarithm $\log$ of [[def-natural-logarithm]]. Unless a base is displayed, every information quantity on this page uses $\ln$ and is measured in **nats**. For a base $b>1$ and $t>0$, define
$$\log_b t:=\frac{\ln t}{\ln b}.$$
The denominator is positive: $b>1$, $\ln$ is strictly increasing, and $\ln 1=0$ by [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]. A base-$b$ entropy or divergence is obtained by replacing each $\ln$ in the finite formulas below by $\log_b$; use $0\log_b0:=0$ and assign $+\infty$ to a positive numerator over a zero denominator. The case $b=2$ measures **bits**; $b=e$ gives nats.
lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal U,\mathcal V$ be finite nonempty alphabets and let $p_{UV}(u,v)\ge0$ satisfy $\sum_{u,v}p_{UV}(u,v)=1$. Define $p_U(u)=\sum_vp_{UV}(u,v)$ and $p_V(v)=\sum_up_{UV}(u,v)$. Then both marginals are probability vectors. For each $v$ with $p_V(v)>0$, the conditional vector $p_{U|v}(u):=p_{UV}(u,v)/p_V(v)$ is a probability vector; likewise for conditioning on positive-mass $u$. Consequently, if $p_{UVW}$ is a finite joint pmf, then for every $w$ with $p_W(w)>0$, $p_{UV|w}$ and its two marginals are probability vectors.
lem-it-finite-kl-agrees-with-measurable-:
## Statement

Assume AC only for the interface to the published general definition [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. Let $p,q$ be probability vectors on a finite set $S$, and let $P(A)=\sum_{i\in A}p_i$, $Q(A)=\sum_{i\in A}q_i$ on $\mathcal P(S)$. Then the measurable-space divergence $D(P\|Q)$ equals the finite KL sum $\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i)$, with value $+\infty$ exactly when some $p_i>0=q_i$.
lem-it-finite-log-sum-inequality:
## Statement

Let $(a_i)_{i=1}^n,(b_i)_{i=1}^n$ be finite nonnegative real vectors, with $A=\sum_i a_i$ and $B=\sum_i b_i$. Interpret $\sum_{a_i>0}a_i\ln(a_i/b_i)$ as $+\infty$ if some $a_i>0=b_i$; otherwise zero coordinates contribute $0$. Interpret $A\ln(A/B)$ as $0$ if $A=0$ and as $+\infty$ if $A>0=B$. Then

$$\sum_{a_i>0}a_i\ln\frac{a_i}{b_i}\ge A\ln\frac AB.$$

When $A,B>0$, equality holds exactly when $a_i=(A/B)b_i$ for every $i$. If $A>0=B$, both sides are $+\infty$ and no finite equality characterization is asserted.
def-it-finite-conditional-entropy:
## Definition

Let $p_{XY}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$. It is the weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Write $p_Y(y)=\sum_xp_{XY}(x,y)$. For each $y$ with $p_Y(y)>0$, set $p_{X|y}(x)=p_{XY}(x,y)/p_Y(y)$; this is a probability vector by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. Define the conditional entropy in nats by

$$H(X|Y):=\sum_{y:p_Y(y)>0}p_Y(y)H(p_{X|y}),$$

where $H(p)=-\sum_xp(x)\ln p(x)$ is the finite entropy of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]]. Terms for zero-mass $y$ are omitted. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$.
def-it-finite-mutual-information:
## Definition

Let $p_{XY}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$, with marginals $p_X(x):=\sum_y p_{XY}(x,y)$ and $p_Y(y):=\sum_xp_{XY}(x,y)$. The marginals are probability vectors by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. The joint vector is the outcome-weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Define mutual information in nats by

$$I(X;Y):=D(p_{XY}\|p_X\otimes p_Y)=\sum_{(x,y):p_{XY}(x,y)>0}p_{XY}(x,y)\ln\frac{p_{XY}(x,y)}{p_X(x)p_Y(y)},$$

where $D$ is the finite KL convention of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] and $(p_X\otimes p_Y)(x,y):=p_X(x)p_Y(y)$. Every ratio in the displayed sum is positive and finite: if $p_{XY}(x,y)>0$, then each marginal sum is at least that positive entry. The sum is over finite support, so $I(X;Y)$ is finite. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$.
def-it-finite-conditional-mutual-informa:
## Definition

Let $p_{XYZ}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets and write $p_Z(z)$ for its marginal. It is the law of finite coordinate random elements on the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]] and [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. For each $z$ with $p_Z(z)>0$, the conditional law $p_{XY|z}$ and its marginals $p_{X|z},p_{Y|z}$ are probability vectors by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. Define conditional mutual information in nats by

$$I(X;Y|Z):=\sum_{z:p_Z(z)>0}p_Z(z)D(p_{XY|z}\|p_{X|z}\otimes p_{Y|z}),$$

using the finite KL convention of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]], where $(p_{X|z}\otimes p_{Y|z})(x,y):=p_{X|z}(x)p_{Y|z}(y)$. A positive conditional joint mass forces both conditional marginals to be positive, so each displayed KL term is finite. Zero-mass conditioning values contribute no term. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$ inside the conditional KL sums.
thm-it-finite-kl-nonnegative-equality:
## Statement

For finite probability vectors $p,q$ on the same alphabet, $D(p\|q)\ge0$, and $D(p\|q)=0$ if and only if $p=q$. If $p_i>0=q_i$ for some coordinate, then $D(p\|q)=+\infty$.
thm-it-information-unit-conversion:
## Statement

For any $b>1$, define each base-$b$ finite information quantity by replacing $\ln$ with $\log_b$ in its defining finite formula. Then

$$H_b(p)=\frac{H(p)}{\ln b},\qquad D_b(p\|q)=\frac{D(p\|q)}{\ln b},$$

where the second equality is in $[0,+\infty]$ and $+\infty/\ln b:=+\infty$. The same conversion holds for finite conditional entropy, mutual information, and conditional mutual information. In particular, values in bits equal nats divided by $\ln2$.
thm-it-finite-conditional-mutual-informa:
## Statement

For finite $X,Y,Z$,

$$I(X;Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|Z)-H(X,Y|Z)\ge0.$$

Equality holds if and only if, for every $z$ with $p_Z(z)>0$, the conditional joint pmf factors as $p_{XY|z}=p_{X|z}p_{Y|z}$; this is conditional independence given $Z$.
thm-it-finite-entropy-chain-rule:
## Statement

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.
thm-it-finite-markov-data-processing:
## Statement

Let $X,Y,Z$ have a joint pmf on finite alphabets and suppose that, for every $y$ with $p_Y(y)>0$,

$$p_{XZ|y}(x,z)=p_{X|y}(x)p_{Z|y}(z).$$

This is the finite Markov condition $X\to Y\to Z$. Then

$$I(X;Z)\le I(X;Y),$$

with equality if and only if $I(X;Y|Z)=0$, equivalently $X$ and $Y$ are conditionally independent given every positive-mass value of $Z$.
thm-it-fano-inequality:
## Statement

Let $X$ take values in an alphabet $\mathcal X$ of size $m\ge2$, let $Y$ be finite, and let $\widehat X$ be an estimator in the same alphabet generated from $Y$, so the joint pmf factors as $p_{XY\widehat X}=p_{XY}p_{\widehat X|Y}$. Put $P_e=\mathbb P[\widehat X\ne X]$ and define

$$h_2(t):=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t),\qquad 0\ln0:=0.$$

Then

$$H(X|Y)\le h_2(P_e)+P_e\ln(m-1)\le \ln2+P_e\ln m.$$

For $m=1$, $X$ is constant and $H(X|Y)=0$.
cor-it-fano-with-erasure-or-out-of-alpha:
## Statement

Let $X$ have a finite alphabet $\mathcal X$ of size $m\ge1$, let $Y$ be finite, and let $\widehat X$ be any finite estimate output generated from $Y$, with an output alphabet that may contain symbols outside $\mathcal X$. Assume $X\to Y\to\widehat X$, and set $P_e=\mathbb P[\widehat X\ne X]$. Use $h_2$ as defined in [[thm-it-fano-inequality]]. Then

$$H(X|Y)\le h_2(P_e)+P_e\ln m.$$

If $X$ is uniform on $\mathcal X$, then

$$ (1-P_e)\ln m\le I(X;Y)+h_2(P_e).$$
